justifications.functional_suitability: Video Media Server, Prescription Integration Service, AI Inference & Audit Service cover R-01 to R-03. Consent has only Consent & Policy Engine and JWT & Consent Validation Filter, with no patient consent management UI or service (R-04). Several flows are missing, and the Core to AI Service relationship is undefined.
justifications.performance_efficiency: Adaptive Bitrate (ABR) Controller, LiveKit SFU, Regional Rate Limiter (Redis), BullMQ queues and Pub/Sub asynchronous processing are concrete mechanisms. No autoscaling, caching of data reads or explicit scalability strategy is shown. The sub-300 kbit/s target is only partly addressed.
justifications.compatibility: Translation & Mapping Engine, HL7 FHIR/national standards labels on Prescription Integration Service, and Pharmacies integration address R-08. However, there are no per-country EU adapters, and the external LLM API and billing integrations are loosely defined. FHIR is not used beyond pharmacy links.
justifications.usability: Patient Portal UI, Clinician Portal UI and Caregivers are served via Web & Mobile Apps with offline-first Local Storage Manager. Auditors have a Report Generation & Dashboard API. No consent management UI, no accessibility or localization, and no degraded-mode UX are described.
justifications.reliability: Circuit Breaker & Fallback Filter, the AI Circuit Breaker & Fallback Policy Engine, BullMQ retries, Regional Dead-Letter Queue, and offline Local Storage Manager provide fault tolerance. No multi-zone redundancy, backup or disaster recovery is shown. Degraded video mode relies on ABR only.
justifications.security: mTLS via Istio, SPIFFE/SPIRE identities, JWT & Consent Validation Filter, CMEK, WORM BigQuery Compliance Data Store, signed audit payloads in Audit Log Formatter & Writer, and PHI-stripped logs are strong. Gaps include the external LLM API receiving potentially regional PHI and an undefined 'Regional Local Vault / Buffer'.
justifications.maintainability: Clear containers and components with distinct responsibilities, an API Gateway filter chain, and a separate Audit & Compliance Reporting Service. Weaknesses include the combined AI Inference & Audit Service, duplicated circuit-breaker logic, inconsistent models (Cloud SQL vs Spanner), and some undefined elements.
justifications.portability: The architecture is GCP-bound (Cloud Spanner/SQL, BigQuery, Pub/Sub, Cloud Endpoints, KMS). Portable pieces include Envoy/Istio, LiveKit, OPA, and containerized services. No abstraction for infrastructure replacement is explicit, though two regions are supported via Regional Databases.

sensitivity_points: Session token validation round trip to Core service
tradeoffs: Central Core validation adds join latency versus security
PERF-01.justification: LiveKit SFU suits scale, but no autoscaling, capacity sizing or join-time mechanism is described. The token check calls Core Telehealth Service synchronously. Plausible but unproven for 5,000 sessions under 10 s.

elements: External AI Inference Provider / LLM API
tradeoffs: External LLM brings flexibility but latency and residency risk
PERF-02.justification: Depends on an external LLM with no stated capacity, autoscaling or queueing for about 14 requests per second. A fallback exists, but a 3 s p95 is unsubstantiated and the audit write is in-line.

sensitivity_points: Offline sync and conflict handling not defined
tradeoffs: Offline PHI storage helps resilience but widens the data-exposure surface
AVAIL-01.justification: ABR and offline-first encrypted local storage address degraded mode and note retention. However, there is no audio-only fallback, reconnection or sync mechanism, and no evidence of note-loss prevention.

sensitivity_points: Single-region US database with no in-region HA or backup
tradeoffs: Strict isolation prevents cross-region failover, reducing availability
AVAIL-02.justification: Residency is preserved through isolation, but no multi-zone HA, backup, restore or DR design exists for us-central1. Meeting a 1-hour restoration is unsupported. The Cloud SQL zonal option is unspecified.

sensitivity_points: Single mapping engine may become a change hotspot
tradeoffs: Central translation simplifies reuse but couples country standards
MOD-01.justification: A dedicated Prescription Integration Service isolates the changes, but there is no pluggable per-country adapter. Changes would likely touch the shared mapping engine and the dispatcher, so confinement to one adapter is not guaranteed.

elements: External AI Inference Provider / LLM API
sensitivity_points: External provider may change model silently
No rollout or rollback mechanism shown
tradeoffs: Strong traceability adds overhead on the inference path
MOD-02.justification: Version tracking and signed audit logs support traceability of recommendations. No release, canary or rollback mechanism is described, and the external LLM may not pin versions. Rollback is unaddressed.

tradeoffs: Strict isolation blocks legitimate cross-border care without a consent flow
SEC-01.justification: Policy checks and consent validation at the gateway and core service support denial, and the audit service logs requests. However, no consent store or defined cross-region access path exists, and there is no explicit logging of denials.

sensitivity_points: No consent store or revocation mechanism modeled
tradeoffs: Embedded policy engine is fast but needs consent state synchronized
SEC-02.justification: Consent is checked at runtime, which could stop sharing, but no per-purpose consent management, research-sharing pipeline or revocation propagation is shown. Verification relies on generic audit logs only.
